- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.5), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.  
- If model forecast mean is significantly below true outcome mean (e.g., > 3% gap over 10+ days), apply a “mean reversion” bias: adjust forecast toward historical average of last 10–15 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period rallies (last 7–10 days of forecast); increase final 5–7 days of forecast by 1–2% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.  
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
